extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, legal researchers, and historians seeking the text of the U.S. Constitution (Article II provisions)
extracted.subtask_description: Transcription of portions of Article II of the U.S. Constitution covering the appointment and voting of electors, presidential qualifications, succession, compensation, oath, and the President's role as commander-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and number of electors
rubrics_metrics.description: Each State shall appoint, in such manner as the legislature thereof may direct, a number of electors equal to the whole number of Senators and Representatives to which the State may be entitled in the Congress; but no Senator or Representative, or person holding an office of trust or profit under the United States, shall be appointed an elector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States determine the manner of appointment by their legislatures; persons who are Senators, Representatives, or hold a federal office of trust/profit are disqualified from being electors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electors' voting method and residency rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The electors shall meet in their respective States, and vote by ballot for two persons, of whom one at least shall not be an inhabitant of the same State with themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electors cast two votes by ballot; at least one of the two persons voted for must not be a resident of the elector's state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and transmission of electoral votes
rubrics_metrics.description: They shall make a list of all the persons voted for, and of the number of votes for each; which list they shall sign and certify, and transmit sealed to the Seat of the government of the United States, directed to the President of the Senate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electors must prepare a signed and certified list showing each person voted for and the vote counts, and transmit it sealed to the federal seat of government addressed to the President of the Senate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening and counting electoral certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the Senate shall, in the presence of the Senate and House of Representatives, open all the certificates, and the votes shall then be counted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President of the Senate opens all received electoral certificates before both houses of Congress and the votes are counted in that joint proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of President by majority and contingency procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The person having the greatest number of votes shall be the President, if such number be a majority of the whole number of electors appointed; and if there be more than one who have such majority, and have an equal number of votes, then the House of Representatives shall immediately choose by ballot one of them for President; and if no person have a majority, then from the five highest on the list the said House shall in like manner choose the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority of appointed electors is required for a candidate to be President. If multiple candidates tie with a majority, the House selects among them. If no candidate has a majority, the House chooses from the top five vote-getters.

rubrics_metrics.name: State voting in House contingent election and quorum/majority requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: But in choosing the President, the votes shall be taken by States, the representation from each State having one vote; a quorum for this purpose shall consist of a member or members from two thirds of the States, and a majority of all the States shall be necessary to a choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a contingent House election, each State delegation casts one collective vote; a quorum requires presence from two-thirds of the states, and a majority of states is needed to elect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vice President determined by elector votes and Senate contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: In every case, after the choice of the President, the person having the greatest number of votes of the electors shall be the Vice President. But if there should remain two or more who have equal votes, the Senate shall choose from them by ballot the Vice President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The elector vote-getter with the next highest (greatest) number of votes becomes Vice President, unless there is a tie among candidates, in which case the Senate selects the Vice President by ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional power to set times for choosing electors and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Congress may determine the time of choosing the electors, and the day on which they shall give their votes; which day shall be the same throughout the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress has authority to fix the date for appointing electors and the uniform day for casting electoral votes nationwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for the office of President
rubrics_metrics.description: No person except a natural born citizen, or a citizen of the United States, at the time of the adoption of this Constitution, shall be eligible to the office of President; neither shall any person be eligible to that office who shall not have attained to the age of thirty five years, and been fourteen years a resident within the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requirements: natural-born citizen (with a transitional clause for those citizens at adoption), at least 35 years old, and 14 years' residency within the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential succession and congressional authority to legislate succession
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of the removal of the President from office, or of his death, resignation, or inability to discharge the powers and duties of the said office, the same shall devolve on the Vice President, and the Congress may by law provide for the case of removal, death, resignation, or inability, both of the President and Vice President, declaring what officer shall then act as President, and such officer shall act accordingly until the disability be removed, or a President shall be elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vice President succeeds on removal, death, resignation, or inability; Congress may by law provide further succession procedures for simultaneous vacancies or disabilities and define who shall act as President until resolution or election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential compensation restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The President shall at stated times, receive for his services, a compensation, which shall neither be increased nor diminished during the period for which he shall have been elected, and he shall not receive within that period any other emolument from the United States or any of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President's salary is fixed for the term (cannot be changed up or down during the term) and the President may not receive other emoluments from the federal government or the states during that term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or affirmation of office
rubrics_metrics.description: Before he enter on the execution of his office, he shall take the following oath or affirmation: 'I do solemnly swear, (or affirm,) that I will faithfully execute the office of President of the United States, and will, to the best of my ability, preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President must take the specified oath or affirmation before executing the office, pledging faithful execution of the office and to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: President as commander-in-chief (role statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: § 2. The President shall be commander-in-chief of the army and ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares the President's role as commander-in-chief of the military (text on page is truncated; later clauses in Article II further define military powers and appointment authorities). Note on page: an amendment later substituted for this paragraph (reference to 12th Amendment is present as editorial note).
